title.en: India: location, physical divisions and rivers

text.en: India lies in the northern and eastern hemispheres, with the Himalayas in the north and ocean on three sides. Few countries have so many kinds of landscape within their borders.

India extends from about 8 degrees 4 minutes N to 37 degrees 6 minutes N latitude, and the Tropic of Cancer passes almost through the middle of the country.
The Indian Standard Meridian is 82.5 degrees E, so Indian Standard Time is 5 hours 30 minutes ahead of Greenwich Mean Time.
The physical divisions are the Northern Mountains (the Himalayas), the Northern Plains, the Peninsular Plateau, the Indian Desert, the Coastal Plains and the Islands.
The Himalayas are young fold mountains with three parallel ranges: Himadri, Himachal and Shiwaliks.
The Northern Plains were built by the alluvium of the Indus, Ganga and Brahmaputra rivers and are fertile.
Himalayan rivers such as the Ganga and Brahmaputra are perennial because snow melts feed them; Peninsular rivers such as the Godavari, Krishna and Kaveri depend on rain and are seasonal.
The Western Ghats and Eastern Ghats meet near the Nilgiris; the Deccan Plateau lies between them.

problem.en: Why is the Ganga flowing all year while the Godavari swells mainly in the monsoon?

text.en: The Ganga is fed both by rain and by melting Himalayan snow.

why.en: Snowmelt keeps the flow in summer.

text.en: The Godavari is a Peninsular river that depends mainly on monsoon rain.
So Himalayan rivers are perennial and Peninsular rivers are seasonal.

prompt.en: Name the physical divisions of India and contrast Himalayan with Peninsular rivers.

commonMisconceptions.en: Thinking all Indian rivers flow all year
